title: How far must output fall?

controls.label: Share of a change in income spent on imports (marginal)

predict.q: The deficit is still 20 bn, but now imports fall by 0.40 for every 1 fall in income, not 0.25. Using expenditure reducing alone, how far must real output fall to close the deficit?

options.fb: 20 ÷ 0.40 = 50: a fall in income of 50 bn cuts imports by 20 bn.

options.s: 80 bn, as before: the deficit is the same size
options.fb: The fall needed depends on the share of income spent on imports, not only on the size of the deficit: 20 ÷ 0.40 = 50.
8 is 20 × 0.40; divide the gap by the share, do not multiply.

options.s: 128 bn: a bigger share spent on imports means a bigger fall
options.fb: The reverse: the bigger the share of each fall in income that comes off imports, the smaller the fall in output needed.

task: Set the share-of-a-change-in-income slider to 0.40, then move the Fall in real output slider and watch real output, imports and the current account. Try other shares.

target.do: Set the share to 0.40 and the fall in AD to 50, then press Check.

takeaway: The smaller the share of extra income spent on imports, the bigger the fall in output needed. Expenditure reducing can be costly.
